The Jigawa State Police Command has presented N20.4m in insurance and welfare benefits to families of officers who died while serving in the force. The cheques, totalling N20,401,267.34, were presented to the next of kin of the deceased officers by the state Commissioner of Police, Tijjani Murtala, at the command headquarters in Dutse on Friday. The payment was made under the Group Life Assurance and the Inspector-General of Police Family Welfare Scheme. Speaking on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, Murtala said the money was intended to support the families of officers who died in active service. “The cheques were meant to support the families of officers who paid the supreme price while serving their fatherland,” he said. Jigawa Hisba handled 5,616 cases in 10 months – Official Bandits kill three, raze entire village in Niger Jigawa police boss begs traditional institutions to address security concerns He also expressed the force’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the deceased officers and assured their relatives that the police remained committed to the welfare of families left behind by personnel who died in service. Murtala urged the beneficiaries to use the financial support judiciously for the benefit of their families. One of the beneficiaries, Dahiru Wambai, who spoke on behalf of the relatives, thanked the Inspector-General and the state police commissioner for the intervention. “We are profoundly grateful to the Inspector-General of Police and the Commissioner of Police for this gesture. It is timely and it will go a long way in supporting the families left behind by our loved ones,” he said. Salisu Kabuga
